clue.text: One whose work could be framed beginning to get less active

definitions.text: One whose work could be framed

indicators.note: beginning to asks for only the opening letter of the word get

parts.note: someone less active is lazier

explanation.surface: Someone at work is told to start taking things easier.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who cuts and fits glass panes, which are then set in window frames, so his work is literally framed.

clue.text: Smirk from unpleasant expert

parts.note: grim means unpleasant
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A nasty specialist wears a smug smile.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose equivalence: both are deliberate facial expressions, here a twisted face put on for effect.

clue.text: Commend a very quiet tailless dog

parts.note: PP is pianissimo, very quiet in music

indicators.note: tailless says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: Rover is a stock name for a dog

explanation.surface: Someone praises a silent dog with no tail.
explanation.definitionFit: To approve of something is to speak well of it, close to commending it.

clue.text: Epic illustration initially kept by painter put up

indicators.note: kept by places the initial letter inside the turned painter
put up in a down clue means the painter's name is written upwards

parts.note: Salvador Dali was a Spanish surrealist painter

indicators.note: initially takes just the first letter of illustration

explanation.surface: An illustration of an epic scene is hung up by the artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns DALI into ILAD, and 'kept by' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's poem about the siege of Troy is a classic example of an epic.

clue.text: Left-winger and German worker no longer operational

parts.note: a red is a socialist or communist
und is German for and
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: A socialist and a German labourer have been laid off.
explanation.definitionFit: Something redundant is surplus to needs, so it is out of use; a worker made redundant has lost the job.

clue.text: Search place linked to gold in river

indicators.note: in tells us the place-and-gold pair sits inside the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
PL is the usual abbreviation for place in street names
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Prospectors hunt for a spot where gold turns up in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To explore an area is to search through it thoroughly; verbs of investigation.

clue.text: Elude first woman holding bill

indicators.note: holding means the woman's name wraps around the bill

parts.note: Eve is the first woman in the Bible
an ad (advertisement) is a bill

explanation.surface: Eve slips away clutching a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to escape or avoid, the same as to elude; synonyms.

clue.text: Flier taking constituent over hill

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the constituent above the hill

parts.note: a part is a constituent
a ridge is a long hill

explanation.surface: A bird flies over a ridge with something in tow.
explanation.definitionFit: A partridge is a game bird, so it is something that flies.

clue.text: First sign of drinks during over in ground — feature of cricket?

indicators.note: during puts the first letter inside the scrambled letters
ground, as in ground down, suggests the letters are broken up and remade
first sign of takes the initial letter of drinks

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: drinks are taken during an over at the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' turns OVERIN into ONRIVE, and 'during' puts D inside. The on drive is a cricket stroke hit straight past the bowler on the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: The on drive is a batting stroke in cricket, one of the game's features.

clue.text: Copper, say, sorting out melee by conservationists

indicators.note: by places the conservationists beside the rearranged letters
sorting out says the letters of melee are rearranged

parts.note: NT is the National Trust, a British conservation charity

explanation.surface: A policeman breaks up a brawl involving environmentalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorting out' turns MELEE into ELEME. 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is a chemical element, and 'say' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Young miscreant was dishonest? It's not obvious

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
someone who was dishonest lied

explanation.surface: A naughty child told a fib, though the evidence is far from clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hinted at rather than stated outright is not plain to see; synonymous adjectives.

clue.text: Shorten amateur golf hosted by woman in match

indicators.note: hosted by puts the golf letter inside the woman being described

parts.note: a bride is the woman in a marriage match
Golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A golf club cuts short an amateur round played with a woman partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' looks sporting next to golf, but here it means a marriage, whose woman is the bride.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten it by cutting parts out; synonyms.

clue.text: Shunning a cove and swimming around island

indicators.note: around says the scrambled letters wrap themselves about the island letter
swimming suggests the letters are moving about freely and rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone keeps away from a bay, swimming round an island instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' turns ACOVEAND into AVODANCE, and 'around' puts that about I.
explanation.definitionFit: Avoidance is the act of keeping away from something, which is what shunning means.

clue.text: Breed fish, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word must be spoken to give the answer's sound

parts.note: rays are flat fish, related to skates

explanation.surface: A fish farmer is said to breed fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise animals is to breed and rear them; synonymous farming verbs.

clue.text: Lament being carried by camel (Egyptian)

indicators.note: being carried by says the answer rides inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A mournful song is borne along on an Egyptian camel.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegy is a poem or song mourning the dead, a formal lament.

clue.text: Champion entering northerly river with suit in maritime group

indicators.note: entering puts the champion letters inside the turned river
northerly in a down clue means the river is written going up

parts.note: the Tay is a river in Scotland
clubs is one of the four suits in cards

explanation.surface: A champion sails up a Scottish river with a crew in matching outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northerly' reverses the river because a down answer is read top to bottom, so going north means upwards; 'suit' is the card suit, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A yacht club is an association of sailing enthusiasts, a group devoted to the sea.

clue.text: Correction made by chaps with time after noon?

indicators.note: after places the chaps and time letters behind the noon piece

parts.note: noon is the end of the morning, read as A.M. plus END
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Some fellows make a fix to the clock after midday.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags 'noon' as a quirky reading: midday is where the morning finishes, so AM + END.
explanation.definitionFit: An amendment is a change made to put something right, a correction to a text or law.

clue.text: Dine fantastically overlooking hotel, place for cooking in Dutch city

indicators.note: overlooking in a down clue puts the rearranged letters above the hotel
fantastically says the letters of dine are wildly rearranged

parts.note: Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an oven is a place for cooking

explanation.surface: Diners eat well at a hotel with a fine kitchen in the Netherlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Eindhoven is a city in the south of the Netherlands, home of Philips and PSV.

clue.text: Trip once organised to tour new US university

indicators.note: to tour means going around, so the rearranged letters enclose the new letter
organised says the letters of trip once are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A trip is arranged once to visit an American campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' turns TRIPONCE into PRICETON, and 'to tour' puts that round N.
explanation.definitionFit: Princeton is an Ivy League university in New Jersey, an example of a US university.

clue.text: Scheme to protect gym below yard — safe site for youngsters?

indicators.note: to protect means the scheme surrounds the pair inside it

parts.note: a plan is a scheme

indicators.note: below in a down clue puts gym under yard

parts.note: PE (physical education) is gym at school

explanation.surface: A plan keeps a playground in the back yard safe for kids.
explanation.definitionFit: A playpen is a small enclosure where a baby can play safely.

clue.text: Examine page penned by six-footer

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed, so the page letter sits inside the creature

parts.note: an insect has six legs, so is a six-footer

explanation.surface: A very tall person looks over a page they have written.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall person, but it is a creature with six feet.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to examine closely; synonyms.

clue.text: Brief communication giving some recurrent thrill — I am elated!

indicators.note: recurrent says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone describes the delight of receiving a short message.
explanation.definitionFit: An email is a short electronic message, a brief communication sent by computer.

clue.text: In the East End, very slender transport company

indicators.note: in London's East End the Cockney accent drops the opening H

parts.note: a hairline crack is very slender

explanation.surface: A thin carrier operates in the East End of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys of London's East End famously drop their aitches.
explanation.definitionFit: An airline is a company that transports passengers by air.

clue.text: Faithful conduct shown by princes, say, after changing sides initially

indicators.note: the first letter swaps right for left, the two sides

parts.note: princes are examples of royalty

explanation.surface: Princes have stayed loyal despite a switch of allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) at the start becomes L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: Loyalty is faithfulness shown in one's behaviour, steadfast allegiance.

clue.text: A second period in court has advantage

parts.note: a set is a period of play on a tennis court

explanation.surface: A tennis player wins the second set and gains the upper hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests law, but it is a tennis court, where play is divided into sets.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful quality or thing that gives you an advantage.

clue.text: Academic companion probing note before violent rally

indicators.note: before places the note piece ahead of the scrambled rally
probing puts the companion letters inside the musical note

parts.note: SO (or SOH) is a note of the sol-fa scale
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

indicators.note: violent suggests the letters of rally are thrown about

explanation.surface: A friend investigates a message sent ahead of a violent protest.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholarly and academic both describe learned, studious work; synonyms.

clue.text: Designate a set of steps for audience

indicators.note: for audience says the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a stile is a set of steps over a fence or wall

explanation.surface: Someone names a staircase for spectators.
explanation.definitionFit: To style someone is to give them a title or name, to designate them.

clue.text: In a while, sound of amusement will banish sound of disgust

indicators.note: will banish means the second sound is driven out of the first

parts.note: laughter is the sound of amusement
ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: Laughter will soon drive out cries of revulsion.
explanation.definitionFit: Later means at some time after now, in a while; synonyms.

clue.text: Singer about to be engulfed by wild yelps

indicators.note: to be engulfed by says the about letters sit inside the scrambled word
wild says the letters of yelps run riot into a new order

parts.note: RE means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A performer is about to be swamped by screaming fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like part of 'about to', but it supplies a piece of its own; 'to be engulfed by' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley was the American rock and roll singer, an example of a singer.

clue.text: Musical group beset by a lot of mean and bitter criticism

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the group sits inside the shortened word
a lot of asks for most but not all of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: vile means mean or despicable
a trio is a group of three musicians

explanation.surface: A band faces harsh and nasty reviews.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitriol is sulphuric acid, and by extension savagely bitter criticism or abuse.

clue.text: Distinguished feature of a cafeteria in demand?

definitions.meaning: distinguished means eminent or worthy of note

definitions.text: feature of a cafeteria in demand?
definitions.meaning: a busy self-service restaurant has every seat taken, so no free table can be found

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into two words describing a crowded canteen.
explanation.definitionFit: Notable means important or eminent, which is what distinguished means of a person.

clue.text: Sister getting really discontented in creche

parts.note: a sister is a senior nurse in a British hospital ward

indicators.note: discontented means emptied of its contents, leaving the outer letters of really

explanation.surface: A nurse is fed up with working in a day-care centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A creche is a place where young children are looked after, as is a day nursery.
